title: Input first, then output
idea: Order matters: you must have the input before you can make the output. Plans run in order.

exercises.prompt: You need the input before you can make the output.
exercises.explanation: You can't toast bread you don't have. Input comes first, output comes after.

exercises.prompt: Put these in the order a task uses them.
exercises.explanation: Input, then the work, then the output. That's the shape of every task.

exercises.prompt: Task: toasting bread. Which comes first?
exercises.explanation: You start with the input — a slice of bread — before any toast can come out.

exercises.prompt: Order these steps for making tea.
blocks: Get a tea bag and hot water (input)
exercises.explanation: Input first, then the work, then the output. Same shape as every task.

exercises.prompt: Instructions in a program also run in order, top to bottom.
exercises.explanation: You learned this in Unit 1: a computer follows steps one by one, in order.

exercises.prompt: Why can't the output come before the input?
options: There would be nothing to make the output from
exercises.explanation: Without the input, there's nothing for the task to work on. No input, no output.

exercises.prompt: Order these for 'add two prices and show the total'.
exercises.explanation: Inputs first (the prices), then the work (adding), then the output (the total).

exercises.prompt: If you try to show a total before you have the prices, the plan is broken.
exercises.explanation: You'd be showing a total you haven't worked out yet. The input has to come first.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to what happens in it.
exercises.explanation: Every task has this shape: input at the start, output at the end, work in between.

exercises.prompt: A tiny program is print("Done"). Which is true about its order?
options: The text Done (input) is given, then it is shown (output)
The output appears before any input
There is no input or output
exercises.explanation: Even the smallest program follows the shape: text in, text shown out.
